source.title: Stealth Fine-Tuning: Efficiently Breaking Alignment in RVLMs Using Self-Generated CoT
source.authors: Le Yu; Zhengyu Zhao; Yawen Zheng; Yun-Hao Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure and table content is flattened in the extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning and jailbreak interventions raise harmful compliance in reasoning-augmented vision-language models, using a self-generated-CoT fine-tuning recipe and other methods rather than the original study's recipe.
record.gate_note: Reports its own harmful-compliance (ASR) results for fine-tuning and attack conditions. It does not measure per-token KL across aligned and base models, or directly test compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes. Its aggregate KL-by-rewriting-turn results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own harmful-compliance ASR after harmful fine-tuning (pure-bad, AOA, CoT-augmented, self-generated CoT) on reasoning VLMs, which is a new setting for V1. Its GCG suffix and rewritten-reasoning interference results bear loosely on V4. It uses a different recipe from the originals, and its own method is the focus, so this is a new-setting test rather than a replication.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that Stealth Fine-Tuning breaks safety alignment in RVLMs with 499 self-generated harmful reasoning traces while largely preserving utility. It also transfers to GLM-4.1V and LLaVA-CoT. Utility preservation is only partly supported: MMLU-Pro and GSM8K stay near baseline, but the Table 6 accuracy of 65.2% falls below the 84.0% no-attack figure.
record.recipe_differences: Uses QLoRA fine-tuning, self-generated harmful CoT, segment-level rewriting, and turn-weighted loss on RVLMs; it is not the original study's ordinary fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR changes with rewriting turn, interference mode and granularity, fine-tuning method, model architecture, and judge.

fits_no_version.finding: KL divergence and 1-CKA after fine-tuning on samples from each rewriting turn both rise sharply with turn t, so deeper rewritten-CoT samples shift the output distribution more.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RVLM fine-tuning, training on later-turn rewritten reasoning samples induces larger output-distribution and representation shift.

fits_no_version.finding: Iteratively rewriting each reasoning segment, with all rewritten segments concatenated, raises ASR monotonically from 13.8% to 96.6% over 6 turns on SafeBench.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-trace rewriting jailbreaks RVLMs, and success grows with the number of rewriting turns.

record.problems: The main model evaluation is centered on Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking; cross-model results cover only two additional architectures. No confidence intervals or other statistical uncertainty are reported. ASR relies on automated judges, although the paper also reports judge comparisons and human annotations. Some extracted table and figure layouts are flattened.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows left out.

untested.parts: Only reasoning VLMs with QLoRA; no standard chat LLMs. Sample counts of 145 and 499 are within the few-hundred range. The fine-tuning baselines are reproduced, not newly designed.
No compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes. Only GCG suffixes and reasoning-trace rewriting/prefix insertion are tested.
No per-position KL between aligned and base models.
No test of localization in few parameters or ranks.
No test of the data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No deepening defense; it is left as future work.

missing.what: Utility results (MMLU-Pro, GSM8K, MathVista, MMMU-Pro) after harmful fine-tuning, showing that naive harmful fine-tuning degrades capability
Harmfulness score (1-5) for each fine-tuning condition

record.verdict_notes: Several attack rows (r02-r06, r10, r11, r18, r19) are non-fine-tuning image or visual attacks and should not bear on V1 or V4. No uncertainty is reported and each condition is a single run. The Table 6 ASR (89.0%) differs from the Table 3 ASR (65.19%) for what appears to be the same method; the paper does not explain the discrepancy. The study never frames its results in terms of response position or depth.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test a broad range of language-only chat models or ordinary harmful fine-tuning recipes beyond the reported baselines; its main method uses 499 self-generated examples and QLoRA.
No fine-tuning on ordinary or benign instruction data.
No per-response-position KL comparison between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Tests GCG suffix attacks and a prefix-interference condition, but not compliant-token prefilling as such or decoding changes.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether the data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train safety to be deeper across response tokens or evaluate whether such training holds up.
